chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Allah, the Exalted, lightened the prayers for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) until they became five prayers, Allah revealed to him: 'O Muhammad, five [prayers] are like fifty [prayers].'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith 'Five as Fifty' regarding daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal elucidates the theological principle of divine grace (fadl) in jurisprudence, illustrating how the burden of fifty daily prayers was reduced to five while retaining their full spiritual merit. It underscores the Shia understanding of the Prophet's unique status and the ease God placed upon the community, reflecting the broader Quranic theme of not burdening souls beyond their capacity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-7 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father (ra) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Himyari quoted Muawiyah ibn Hakeem, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abil Hassan al-Azdi that Abi Abdullah (AS) said,
“When the Honorable the Exalted God lightened the prayers to five units for the Prophet (sw), God revealed to him, ‘O Muhammad! Five is as fifty.’”
